notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 41%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Lian Bichsel is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games.
Miro Heiskanen returned in their last game after missing 5 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Kyle Burroughs was added to the roster on Nov 15 and has played beside Trey Taylor.

Noah Hanifin is out week to week and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Parker Wotherspoon has taken his spot beside Dylan Coghlan. That pair has had 65% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 52:42 together, up from 43% with Hanifin.

story.head: Johnston’s favorite opponent
paras: The Stars already played in Vegas once this season and left with a 4-3 overtime win on Tuesday. The Golden Knights are winless in three (0-1-2), while the Stars have won three straight. Going in, the Stars are second in the Central (tenth in the NHL) and the Golden Knights second in the Pacific (tied for fourth).

This season, the Stars have outscored teams 59-51, even though they’ve been outscored 38-36 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 13-8, and no team creates more chances on the power play. This season, the Golden Knights have outscored teams 76-65, but only 47-43 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 23-16.

The Stars block more shots than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd). The Golden Knights, by contrast, draw more penalties than they take (1st). Dallas has allowed 2.43 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. As for the Knights, they create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd). They also have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), and the Stars’ power play against their penalty killers is strength against strength. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Stars (lowest), so expect a tight one.

Mikko Rantanen (10 G / 16 A / 26 P in 21 GP) leads the Stars in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and five goals in seven games against Vegas since 2023-24. Jason Robertson (10 G / 14 A / 24 P in 21 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Golden Knights, Jack Eichel (9 G / 19 A / 28 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, with six goals in ten games against Dallas since 2023-24. Mark Stone (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 23 GP) has a team-high eleven goals.
Jake Oettinger (11-4-1 / .901 SV% in 16 GS) is expected to start for Dallas, and Adin Hill (7-2-2 / .901 SV% in 11 GS) for Vegas.
At home, Ryan Craig likes to send Lavoie, Dowd and Bowman out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Blackwell, Faksa and Perron.
